sources.name: Institute for the Study of War
sources.tagline: Reliable research, analysis, and innovative technology to enhance national security.
sources.description: ISW is a non-partisan, non-profit, public policy research organization advancing an informed understanding of military affairs through reliable research, trusted analysis, and innovative education. ISW produces daily open-source intelligence assessments of ongoing conflicts.
sources.license_note: Data summarized from public ISW reports. Full reports and maps at understandingwar.org.

sources.name: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project
sources.tagline: The highest-quality and most widely used near-real-time source on political violence and protest data worldwide.
sources.description: ACLED is an independent, impartial conflict monitor providing real-time data and analysis on political violence and protest in all countries and territories across the world. Coverage spans 190+ countries with event-level data going back to 1997 for Africa.
sources.license_note: ACLED data is licensed. Summarized statistics presented under fair use. Full data at acleddata.com.

sources.name: Live Universal Awareness Map
sources.tagline: Leading independent global news and information site dedicated to factual reporting of conflicts, human rights issues, protests, terrorism, and more.
sources.description: LiveUAMap is a geolocated editorial aggregation platform displaying relevant events in near-real-time on interactive maps. Created in February 2014 by Ukrainian software engineers, it expanded from monitoring the Russo-Ukrainian War to covering 60+ regional and thematic maps globally. Used by the UN, MSF, The Guardian, and ACLED.
sources.license_note: Event data via LiveUAMap API (GeoJSON). Free tier covers primary regions; Pro/Enterprise for full archive.

sources.name: WAR-RADAR
sources.tagline: Real-time global war and armed conflict monitor powered by AI analysis of news articles.
sources.description: WAR-RADAR ingests from 15 RSS feeds, NewsAPI, and GDELT, filtering through 60+ conflict keywords. AI (GPT-4o-mini) extracts and geolocates conflict zones, classifying them into 7 conflict types and 4 severity tiers. Aims for 15-30 distinct conflict zones per scan.

sources.name: WAR WATCH — World Assessment and Tracking of Civilian Harm
sources.tagline: Tracking and assessing armed conflicts and civilian harm under international humanitarian law.
sources.description: Operated by the Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights. Launched December 2025, integrating the RULAC project (active since 2007) and IHL in Focus (2023). Provides legal classification of armed conflicts and IHL compliance assessment of civilian harm. Funded by EU ECHO and Swiss SDC.

sources.name: War Monitor
sources.tagline: Real-time global conflict intelligence platform with AI-powered event classification.
sources.description: War Monitor ingests breaking news from BBC World, Al Jazeera, Reuters, and Telegram OSINT channels, geolocates events on a 3D globe, and uses AI to classify and severity-score events (1-10). Features conflict thread grouping and daily intel briefings.

sources.name: War.Direct
sources.tagline: Non-commercial OSINT aggregation platform tracking the US/Israel vs Iran & Axis of Resistance conflict since Day 1.
sources.description: Co-built by Rishi Khiani and Claude (Anthropic), War.Direct tracks the US/Israel vs. Iran conflict that began Feb 28, 2026. Features a 12-section war report card with verified casualties, military scoreboard, war crimes documentation, coalitions, and global ripple effects. Has informed 2,000,000+ people.
sources.license_note: Non-commercial, open-source intelligence. Data at war.direct.

sources.name: Telegram Archive of the War
sources.tagline: Emergency archiving of Telegram channels and chats documenting Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
sources.description: Initiated by the Center for Urban History (Lviv, Ukraine) and coordinated by Taras Nazaruk. Archive of 2,711 Telegram items (1,048 channels, 1,651 chats, 12 chatbots) totaling 27.8 TB. Covers February 24, 2022 to June 2023. Documents Ukrainian society during wartime including propaganda, volunteer coordination, personal diaries, and information warfare.
sources.license_note: Non-commercial research only. Access requires researcher agreement. Data at telegram.lvivcenter.org.

theaters.name: Russia & Ukraine
theaters.summary: Full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine entered a new phase. Ukraine launched an intermediate-range strike campaign alongside new mechanized attacks. Civilian casualties reached their highest level since 2022. Russia continues to expand its footprint in Africa through proxy forces.

key_developments.text: Daily Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment published with frontline updates.
ISW analyst discusses Ukraine's battlefield momentum in Atlantic Council media appearance.
ISW briefs Helsinki Commission on Russia's exploitation and engagement in Africa.
CNN reports highest civilian casualties since 2022 as bombardment intensifies.

featured_reports.title: Ukraine's Intermediate-Range Strike Campaign and New Mechanized Attacks Herald the Start of a New Phase of the War

theaters.name: US/Israel vs Iran & Axis of Resistance
theaters.summary: Full-scale conflict between US/Israel and Iran & the Axis of Resistance since February 28, 2026 (Day 164). Includes airstrikes on Iran, Hezbollah ground war in Lebanon, Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, Gulf state strikes, and militia attacks on US bases. A collapsed ceasefire (Apr 7 - Jul 9) reignited full-scale war.

theaters.name: China & Taiwan
theaters.summary: Ongoing strategic competition in the Taiwan Strait and broader Indo-Pacific. North Korea's constitutional amendments cement the regime's strategic posture. ISW tracks Chinese coercion, North Korean provocations, and alliance dynamics across East Asia.

key_developments.text: Latest China & Taiwan Update published tracking cross-strait activity.
North Korea's constitutional amendments cement the regime's strategic posture.

featured_reports.title: North Korea's Constitutional Amendments Cement the Regime's Strategic Posture

theaters.name: Adversary Entente Task Force
theaters.summary: Dedicated task force tracking the deepening alignment of the axis of adversaries — Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea. Analysis covers strategic coordination, sanctions evasion, arms transfers, and each actor's calculations as the bloc confronts the US-led order.

latest_report.title: Russia's Non-Response to US Actions in Venezuela Reveal a Kremlin Balancing Act

key_developments.text: Russia's non-response to US actions in Venezuela reveals a Kremlin balancing act between partners.

theaters.name: Cognitive Warfare
theaters.summary: Tracking information operations, propaganda, and media manipulation — primarily Kremlin-linked. The Kremlin's expanding media conglomerate spreads across multiple platforms and languages, laundering narratives through co-opted outlets and influence networks.

key_developments.text: Major report maps the Kremlin's expanding media conglomerate and influence networks.

theaters.name: Contemporary & Future War
theaters.summary: Emerging military technology and strategic studies. Lessons from Ukraine's drone and mechanized warfare are reshaping doctrine. ISW analyzes how battlefield innovations — FPV drones, intermediate-range strikes, electronic warfare — define the future of conflict.

latest_report.title: Ukraine's Intermediate-Range Strike Campaign and New Mechanized Attacks Herald the Start of a New Phase of the War

key_developments.text: New phase of the war marked by Ukraine's intermediate-range strike campaign and mechanized attacks.

theaters.name: Sudan Civil War
theaters.summary: War between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023. At least 59,000 killed. One of the world's deadliest active conflicts with mass displacement, ethnic violence in Darfur, and famine conditions.

key_developments.text: Sudan remains the 2nd most deadly conflict in the world per ACLED data.
Three-year anniversary of the RSF-SAF conflict. Famine conditions spread.

theaters.name: Myanmar Civil War
theaters.summary: Following the 2021 military coup, Myanmar collapsed into a fragmented civil war with 1,200+ distinct armed groups. Over 100,000 killed since the coup. The most fragmented conflict in the world per ACLED.

key_developments.text: 1,200+ distinct armed groups make Myanmar the world's most fragmented conflict.

theaters.name: Gaza & Palestine
theaters.summary: Israel-Gaza conflict with devastating civilian toll. Palestine contributes over 40% of all global conflict events recorded by ACLED (shared with Ukraine). Most geographically diffuse conflict with ~70% of Gaza/West Bank affected.

key_developments.text: Palestine remains the most geographically diffuse conflict globally per ACLED.

theaters.name: Haiti Gang Crisis
theaters.summary: Armed gangs control large portions of Port-au-Prince. Over 4,500 killed by political violence with near-doubling of fatalities. 50+ armed groups operate across the country.

key_developments.text: Over 4,500 killed by political violence; fatalities nearly doubled.

theaters.name: Sahel Insurgency
theaters.summary: Jihadist insurgencies across the Sahel region. Military coups in Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. Russian/Wagner influence expanding. Mass displacement and civilian targeting.

key_developments.text: Sahel insurgency continues amid political instability and foreign fighter presence.
